concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Project Kingdom gameplay visual-target mockup, one finished wide 16:9 frame.
Reference image 1: CAMERA AND GAMEPLAY LAYOUT ONLY. It is the current prototype. Preserve this elevated orthographic isometric gameplay viewpoint, approximate scene scale, street direction, and readable character scale. Do not copy its pixel sprites, crude meshes, noisy ground or large debug HUD.
Reference image 2: ART DIRECTION ONLY. Carry its original warm painted anime town, cream plaster, blue slate roofs, teal shutters, expressive anthropomorphic animals, gentle summer sunlight, painted foliage and affectionate lived-in detail into the gameplay camera.
Primary request: show how our cat-versus-dogs action RPG would actually LOOK DURING PLAY with the new hand-painted anime art, with the cozy environmental appeal of Ni no Kuni's town exploration but an entirely original place and cast.
CAMERA IS ESSENTIAL: a fixed elevated orthographic/isometric view, camera looking down about 35 degrees from a three-quarter azimuth, matching reference 1. No horizon, no visible sky, no ground-level cinematic view, no wide-angle lens, no converging verticals. See building roofs and two walls. One coherent ground grid and one consistent camera for every building and character. Fill the frame with the neighborhood; do not draw an isolated floating diorama.
Scene: a warm afternoon neighborhood street running diagonally across the middle, cream two-storey cottage in the upper-left/middle, welcoming one-storey Garden Hall with a blue-and-ivory awning in the upper-right, a little notice board between them. Paved sidewalks, low garden walls and a white picket fence, dappled tree shadows, abundant hydrangeas and daisies, iron streetlamps, a modest red postbox, one parked tiny vintage car near the far edge. Dense painted trees and gardens frame the town. Preserve open walkable ground across the central street and the lower sidewalk.
Characters: main player is a small bipedal orange tabby CAT warrior, cream muzzle, red neckerchief, cream tunic with a simple brown leather vest and light shoulder protection, short sword and modest red-and-gold shield. One friendly cat guard nearby. Three readable DOG opponents in blue jackets with light armor and blue-and-gold shields stand at separated positions across the street, facing toward the player, a poised encounter without gore. Original clean-lined, softly cel-shaded anime drawings, around three-and-a-half heads tall, physically integrated with contact shadows. Player is about 8–10 percent of total frame height, near lower-middle-left. Do not use pixel-art sprites, human substitutes, oversized character portraits or copied franchise characters.
ART: painterly anime game environment, watercolor/gouache textures and delicate drawing, appealing rounded natural foliage, calm broad color masses, warm sun against cool green-blue shade. Painted surface detail, not glossy CGI, not photorealistic. Houses are upright, carefully constructed and aligned with the street, not crooked or warped. Focus on a beautiful believable game view with legible gameplay space rather than tiny clutter everywhere.
HUD: a compact tasteful cream-and-dark-teal player plate at the upper-left, with a small original cat face portrait, a slim red health bar and exact text "8 / 8". A small understated location caption at upper center with exact text "GARDEN STREET". Three tiny control prompts at the bottom edge: "WASD  Move", "SPACE  Attack", "SHIFT  Run". UI occupies less than 8 percent of the frame. No big title, FPS/debug text, logo, watermark, skill wheels, dramatic cinematic framing, panels or split screen. This is a concept mockup, not a photograph or an actual engine screenshot.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Project Kingdom gameplay visual-target concept, one wide landscape frame approximately 16:9.
Input image 1 is the authoritative ART, CAMERA, CHARACTER-SCALE AND HUD REFERENCE. Create a new gameplay moment and location in the same game, not a cosmetic edit of that street image.
Maintain the exact elevated orthographic/isometric three-quarter camera of the reference, looking down roughly 35 degrees. No visible sky or horizon, no vanishing point, no ground-level or cinematic viewpoint, no perspective zoom. Roofs and two walls are visible on buildings. Use one consistent ground grid, upright verticals and physically coherent architecture. The world extends past every frame edge; this is not a floating miniature diorama.
Keep the original painterly anime town identity: cream plaster, teal shutters, blue slate roofs, blue-and-ivory awnings, warm stone pavements, lush hand-painted trees, garden flowers, vintage everyday details, delicate linework, gouache/watercolor surfaces and gentle cel-shaded characters. Broad legible play surfaces with intricate detail reserved for borders and architectural focal points. The cozy hand-painted charm of Ni no Kuni's town exploration is the tonal inspiration, but all architecture, characters, UI and locations are original.
Characters must match the reference: small bipedal orange tabby cat player, cream muzzle, red neckerchief, cream shirt, brown leather vest/satchel, olive trousers, short sword and red faction details; a friendly cat guard has a modest red-and-gold shield. Dog enemies wear blue jackets with light protection and carry blue-and-gold shields. They are appealing clean-lined, softly cel-shaded anime figures about 3.5 heads tall. Player occupies 8–10 percent of total screen height. No humans, pixel sprites, oversized portraits in the playfield, franchise characters, photorealism, glossy CGI or voxel art.
HUD styling matches the reference: compact cream-trimmed dark-teal player plate and small cat portrait upper left, thin red health bar; a small tasteful location/objective plate upper center; minimal control prompts lower-left: "WASD  Move", "SPACE  Attack", "SHIFT  Run". HUD must leave the environment and fight legible; no debug text, frame-rate claim, logo, watermark, dialogue boxes, invented skill wheels, title screen, collage or split screen.

Scene and gameplay moment: a small, welcoming community-hall courtyard becomes a contested capture objective. The original Garden Hall sits in the upper-right, recognizable from the reference through cream walls, blue slate roof and striped awning, now opening onto a broad warm-stone public square. A low circular fountain and flower planter occupy the upper-left edge, a community noticeboard and bench rest beside the hall, trimmed hedges and old iron lamps line the perimeter. Leave a genuinely open paved fighting area in the middle and lower half. The garden and town continue beyond the frame; no castle or fortress.
The cat player near the lower-middle is mid-swing against one dog with a raised shield, with a single restrained warm-white painted sword arc and a few small contact sparks. The player's face is visible in three-quarter profile. One friendly cat guard holds a position behind the player; two additional blue dog enemies approach from separated sides, leaving understandable movement lanes. Pose all animals as actively grounded game characters, not a staged character lineup. No gore.
A thin blue circular capture boundary is painted onto the ground outside the hall entrance, projected as a convincing ellipse by the same camera. One dog steps into this ring, so capture is contested; this is a ground marker, not a giant magical effect or glowing platform. Let red/blue team accents and clear silhouettes explain the encounter.
HUD exact text: player health "6 / 8"; upper-center objective "RETAKE GARDEN HALL"; a small status immediately below it "CONTESTED". The action remains the focal point.
Lighting: golden late-afternoon sun, soft blue-green shadows and dappled leaves, inviting and luminous despite the small skirmish. An anime action-RPG gameplay concept, visually practical and readable rather than a dramatic cinematic battle.

Scene and gameplay moment: exploratory travel along the river just beyond our cozy town, at the SAME CLOSE ISOMETRIC GAMEPLAY SCALE as the reference. This is a traversable neighborhood-sized scene, NOT a distant valley panorama or an overhead map.
A gently curving stone-and-earth path passes a small cream cottage with teal shutters and blue slate roof in the upper-left. A clear painted stream winds diagonally down the right half; a low stone footbridge crosses it in the middle-right, leading to an old blue-roofed watermill and fenced kitchen gardens at the upper-right. Two blue dog patrols wait beyond the far end of the bridge as a gentle hint of the next encounter, with the approach still open and clearly navigable. Contact shadows integrate the characters.
